tier_reason: Tier unchanged (C), speed claim marked obsolete. Enricher e116 (2026-10-05) found imgdiff PR #5 (by the odiff author, January 2021): odiff v2 1.194 s vs imgdiff 1.146 s on the cypress pair (parity, imgdiff multi-threaded) and imgdiff single-thread 2.616 s (odiff 2.19x faster); the README's 4.49x/3.15x was against odiff v1, whose dependency did 'massive data copying'. Also a correctness bug in pkg/yiq/delta.go (uint8(r) on 16-bit RGBA() keeps the low byte, wrong for JPEG, 16-bit and semi-transparent pixels), which does not affect the README numbers (all four benchmark PNGs are 8-bit RGBA with alpha 255).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Obsolete: README (2020-2021) cypress image imgdiff 1.442 s vs odiff v1 6.475 s (4.49x), water image 1.908 s vs 6.016 s (3.15x), '3X faster'. imgdiff PR #5 (odiff author, January 2021) on the same cypress pair: odiff v2 1.194 s vs imgdiff 1.146 s (parity, imgdiff on all cores) and imgdiff single-thread 2.616 s, so odiff v2 is about 2.19x faster per thread (derived from page data). No measurement against the current Zig/SIMD odiff.
corrections.baseline: odiff v1 (2020); PR #5 re-measured against odiff v2
corrections.caveats: Speed claim obsolete: the README's 4.49x/3.15x was against odiff v1, whose dependency did 'massive data copying'; imgdiff PR #5 by the odiff author (January 2021) shows parity against odiff v2 on the cypress pair (1.194 s vs 1.146 s) with imgdiff single-thread at 2.616 s, and odiff has since been rewritten in Zig with SIMD. Multi-core vs single-thread: pkg/imgdiff/imgdiff.go splits rows over runtime.NumCPU() goroutines and decodes both PNGs concurrently, while odiff is single-threaded. Different output work (imgdiff writes a transparent red mask with png.BestSpeed; odiff overlays the base image). In the benchmark-era build (1be7ce7) main.go left through os.Exit(1), skipping deferred Flush/Close, so every diff PNG was truncated until 2021-03-25 (the README download link still points to the buggy v1.0.0; fix in v1.0.2, issue #8). Correctness bug: pkg/yiq/delta.go applies uint8(r) to 16-bit RGBA() values, keeping the low byte, which is wrong for JPEG, 16-bit and semi-transparent pixels (the four benchmark PNGs are 8-bit RGBA with alpha 255, so the README numbers are unaffected); a larger compare image with a matching overlap reports equal (#13); --diff-image leaves holes. No anti-aliasing detection; generic image.At pixel access. Benchmark code is not in the repo; toolchain and flags unstated. Last commit 2021-03-25.
